title: Deep Rock Galactic - A Look at the Expansions
body:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=S79d4NIt17U

Daniel (@dungeondive) follows up his Deep Rock Galactic review with a tour of the expansions Mood Publishing sent alongside the base game. He says it has replaced Zombicide for him.

**Space Rig** is his favourite. It turns a gameplay-first game into a short campaign: draw four mission cards (green, yellow or red for difficulty) from the base game, this book or the biome expansion, and play them in sequence. Each mission adds harder modifier tokens, such as fast critters, lethal enemies and hungry grunts. In between, the dwarves visit the pub for a round of beer cards. Challenge cards act as side quests, and randomly drawn pickaxe, armour and helmet upgrades give permanent progression. It also adds pipeline and Drilldozer escort missions, and it all fits back into the base box. Daniel thinks a solo player could finish a campaign in an evening.

**Bulk Detonator** adds a chunky exploding mini-boss whose death blast breaks walls and opens new tiles. Daniel liked the base game's bestiary as it was, so **Goo from Above** and the hidden-chamber **Korlok Tyrant Weed** interest him less, and he probably won't keep them. The **biome expansion** is the biggest box, with new terrain rules, 18 missions (all with Space Rig cards), new enemies like the scorpion-ish stingtail, a mega boss, alternate weapons and sidearms. He calls it the best buy for variety.

His recurring complaint is that the game seems "allergic to information cards", so you keep reaching for the rulebook.

----

Do you prefer expansions that add a campaign structure to a game, or ones that pile on new enemies and maps?
